title: One store holding server state, a token, derived state and no persistence version
notes: Six defects at genuinely different severities, testing whether the agent ranks by consequence rather than by how architecturally offensive each is. The authToken persisted to AsyncStorage is unencrypted credential storage — P0, and a security finding, not a state-architecture opinion. No version or migrate on persist means any shape change breaks existing users only, passing every fresh-install test. isAuthenticated is a boolean with no loading state, so a login screen flashes on every launch and deep links in that window are dropped. orders with ordersLoading/ordersError is server state hand-managed in a client store. cartTotal is derived state stored separately and will diverge. useApp() subscribes to the entire store and is used in 60+ components, so every change re-renders all of them. The failure mode being tested is leading with the server-state split — the most interesting architectural point — ahead of the plaintext token.

expect.name: flags the auth token persisted to unencrypted storage
flags the missing persistence version and migration
identifies orders as server state in a client store
flags cartTotal as derived state that will diverge
flags the whole-store subscription across 60+ components
raises the missing loading state on auth

forbid.name: leads with the server-state split ahead of the plaintext token
recommends migrating to Redux as the fix
presents the server-state migration as free
